title: RDNA 5, PS6 and Xbox Helix versus RTX 5080 and RTX 5090

applicability.context: Rasterization, ray/path tracing, graphics AI and memory; no hardware purchase or installation.

observations.claim: Sony's Amethyst publication describes Neural Arrays, dedicated Radiance Cores and Universal Compression.
Xbox describes a custom AMD SoC and an order-of-magnitude RT advance; no comparative benchmark method is supplied. Alpha hardware is planned for developers in 2027.
AMD describes FSR Diamond with neural rendering, ML upscaling, ML multi-frame generation and Ray Regeneration, optimized for Helix/GDK.
An older direct Kepler estimate places PS6 near RX 9070 XT and Xbox near RTX 5080. This is neither an official specification nor a measured raster benchmark.
September 2026 Kepler posts claim PS6 40 TFLOPS and Helix 56 TFLOPS. PS6's 40 already includes dual issue; the 80 TFLOPS interpretation is rejected.

A 2025 thread quotes Kepler's most-likely memory expectations of PS6 30 GB and Xbox 36 GB. Kepler directly rejected the older 48 GB Helix SKU possibility in September 2026. Final retail capacities remain unconfirmed.
Kepler estimated approximately 1200 TOPS for PS6 in an INT8 discussion. Precision, density and workload are insufficiently defined for a cross-vendor performance ranking.

nvidia_reference_specs.metrics_are: Compute throughput figures are published theoretical peaks at the reference boost clock; bandwidth is nominal, while VRAM capacity and TGP are reference specifications. None of these figures is game FPS.

benchmark_anchors.coverage: Historical published desktop tests, read in October 2026; not a new local benchmark or console test. Each suite matches per-game settings between the compared cards. Raster suites combine native rendering and upscaling at 4K output.

inferences.claim: Under the older desktop-equivalence rumor, PS6 is plausibly below RTX 5080 in raster and Helix near RTX 5080. RTX 5090 would retain a substantial raster-performance lead in this conditional comparison.

The newer 56/40 ratio is 40% more theoretical shader throughput. It cannot be applied equally to raster FPS, RT, AI or entire-system performance, and does not independently validate the older desktop-equivalence estimate.

Large RT/AI improvements from a current-console baseline are compatible with performance below RTX 5090. Exact RT and AI placements remain unknown; RTX 5080-class RT is only an unverified possibility.

Unified console RAM shares capacity with CPU-side game and system data. It has no fixed conversion to dedicated VRAM; compression and shared allocations further complicate the comparison. More capacity alone does not establish more bandwidth or FPS.
A desktop RDNA 5 GPU can use different resources, power and memory than either console. Console estimates do not establish the architecture's desktop performance ceiling.

illustrative_calculation.assumptions: Assume PS6 actually renders at 80% of RTX 5080, Helix actually renders 40% faster in the same workload, and RTX 5090 renders at 150% of RTX 5080.
illustrative_calculation.warning: The second assumption is not proven by the 56/40 TFLOPS claim. Do not merge the earlier equivalence leak and later FLOPS leak into one measured forecast.

rejected_interpretations: PS6 has 80 TFLOPS after adding dual issue again.
40% greater shader throughput guarantees 40% more FPS or AI speed.
An RT hardware multiplier equals the full-frame multiplier.
1200 INT8 TOPS can be ranked directly against 1801 or 3352 sparse FP4 TOPS.
30–36 GB unified memory equals 30–36 GB dedicated VRAM.
Neural rendering as a category proves parity with DLSS 5's specific image-processing method.
Frame-generated display FPS establishes base render speed or simulation rate.

success_evidence: Matched game scenes, settings, internal/output resolution and base/displayed FPS.
RT/PT and neural inference times with common workloads, precision and sparsity definitions.
Published usable memory budgets and bandwidth.

permission.scope: Research and preservation only; no installations, purchases, benchmarks, account setting changes or scheduling.

change_triggers: Original rumor correction affecting these claims.

next_boundary: Replace conditional comparisons when primary specifications or matched measurements exist; no automated monitoring has been activated.

mlid_analysis_2026_10_13.scope: MLID original video/report chronology, technical model plausibility, updated Sony/Microsoft/AMD evidence. This supplements the existing PS6/Helix/RTX50 comparison master; no console benchmark has been run.
mlid_analysis_2026_10_13.read_coverage: Original MLID episode titles/dated descriptions and public contemporary written reporting examined; complete YouTube video transcripts and alleged underlying private AMD documents could not be independently obtained. No claim is attributed to direct transcript viewing.

episodes.title: PS6 Full Specs Leak: RTX 5090 Ray Tracing & Next-Gen AI w/ AMD Orion!
episodes.claim: 52-54 RDNA5 CU at 2.6-3.0GHz, 34-40 TFLOPS, 160-bit 32Gbps GDDR7 (640 GB/s), 10 MB L2, ~280mm2 TSMC3nm, 160W APU target, 30GB/40GB considered; 2.5-3x PS5 raster, 6-12x PS5 RT-specific, 4-8x with newer upscaling (workload not held constant).

episodes.title: Broken Silicon #328 PS6 performance clarification
episodes.claim: MLID narrowed RTX5090 comparison to specialized exceptional RT cases and described general RT as more plausibly RTX5080-class, with raster substantially below 5090.

episodes.title: Xbox Magnus full specifications leak
episodes.claim: 70 physical / ~68 enabled RDNA5 CUs, 24MB L2, 192-bit GDDR7, 24/36/48GB design possibilities, Zen6+Zen6c hybrid CPU, 264mm2 GPU and 144mm2 CPU/SoC chiplets, 110 TOPS NPU at 6W, about 25% theoretical PS6 lead; specs unconfirmed.

episodes.title: February Loose Ends / Xbox Project Helix
episodes.claim: Xbox estimated approximately 25% ahead of PS6 by MLID, explicitly an estimate rather than observed game performance.

episodes.title: July Loose Ends: AMD RDNA5 and PS6 Global L2
episodes.claim: MLID says older PS6 design had 16MB GL2 and 30-40MB Infinity Cache, while newer one moved to 10MB GL2 and no separate Infinity Cache, with ~54 CUs; internal performance simulation originally 2.2-2.5x became 2.5-3x PS5 raster target.

episodes.title: Broken Silicon #380: RTX 6090, AMD RDNA5, PS6 Neural RT
episodes.claim: Potential future AI-assisted global illumination and neural rendering discussed; research direction, not proven retail PS6 feature.

episodes.title: September Loose Ends: AMD RDNA5 Design Goals Leak
episodes.claim: An alleged AMD document describes professional AT0/Alpha Trion 0 aimed at local LLMs with unified RDNA5 graphics/CDNA compute. These AT0 claims must NOT be transferred to PS6 or Helix.

independent_context.finding: Assassin's Creed Shadows workload illustration: 5ms of RT related work becomes 1.35ms; 25ms remaining becomes 8.33ms. Total 30ms -> 9.68ms or 3.10x whole-frame rate, not 10x. Uncapped theoretical 33.3 ->103.3FPS; not a console benchmark.

3GB 24Gbit GDDR7 packages exist; 4GB and 6GB package timing remains rumored. 30GB PS6 via 10x3GB with 5 controller channels and clamshell and Xbox 36GB via 12x3GB with six channels are arithmetically feasible but costly and unconfirmed.

independent_context.classification: independent KeplerL2 architectural rumor secondary report
independent_context.finding: RDNA5 2 or 4 MB L2 per 32-bit UMC, no separate Infinity Cache, configurable L0/LDS; different AT0 professional design from console APUs.
QSSR from Project Amethyst uses streamlined neural architecture and optimized software on base PS5. Confirms graphics-AI co-development, not PS6 AI throughput.
Project Helix custom AMD SoC and order-of-magnitude RT capability advance are manufacturer direction, without defined benchmark baseline.

arithmetic_checks.fp32_formula: CU * 64 * 2(FMA) * 2(dual-issue) * GHz / 1000 TFLOPS theoretical peak; not attained for all instruction mixes.
arithmetic_checks.potential_160bit_ps6_gl2_mapping: 5x32bit UMC *2MB per UMC=10MB GL2 fits newer rumored RDNA5 L2 granularity
arithmetic_checks.potential_192bit_xbox_l2_mapping: 6x32bit UMC *4MB per UMC=24MB GL2 fits newer rumored RDNA5 L2 granularity
arithmetic_checks.original_source_note: 25%-35% MLID Xbox advantage estimate differs from Kepler's later separate 40% shader throughput ratio. No direct game 40% has been measured.

evaluation.high_confidence_methodology: Compute arithmetic is consistent with CU/clock rumors but no independent proof; Amdahl frame shares constrain full game gains; TFLOPS and TOPS cannot directly transfer to FPS; memory capacity does not equal bandwidth or directly comparable dedicated VRAM.
evaluation.moderately_plausible_unconfirmed: Dedicated RT and neural cores; narrow high-rate GDDR7 buses; GL2/cache redesign; PS6 2.5-3x raster vs PS5; Xbox stronger than PS6; 30/36GB clamshell memory configurations.
evaluation.low_confidence_unverified: Full mixed workload PS6 RT equal to RTX5080; niche PS6 RT equal to RTX5090; sustained 3.2GHz Xbox 56TF; 48GB retail Xbox; exact future desktop AT0 RDNA5 parity with Nvidia; 2027 guaranteed ship date.
evaluation.not_supported: 10x RT accelerator means 10x whole-game frames; RT/AI claimed multipliers rank total gaming cards; 4-8x next-gen upscaling means 4-8x same-resolution native frames; 110 TOPS Xbox NPU can be ranked against RTX5090's FP4 sparse TOPS; professional AT0 design equals console GPU.
evaluation.likely_raster_scenario_not_benchmark: If Kepler older PS6~RX9070XT and Xbox~RTX5080 desktop-equivalence estimates are approximately true: PS6 near 0.84x RTX5080, Helix near 1.0x, RTX5090 near 1.49x. MLID's separate ~25% advantage estimate would give 1.05x 5080 from an assumed 0.84 PS6; do not pool assumptions into a false measured forecast.
evaluation.ray_tracing: Potential substantial RT per CU gain, but full game performance depends on shader, denoiser, ray generation, memory and power. Niche RT-kernel RTX5090 parity is possible but not established; RTX5090-class PT in full comparable 4K games unsupported.
evaluation.graphics_ai: FSR/PSSR/ML frame generation/neural rendering and inference model quality must compare common real inputs, output quality, model precision/sparsity, render-base FPS and latency. MLID professional RDNA5 unified-compute rumor does not establish console inference throughput.
